$comment: ASSET CLOSURE - the denominator that comes BEFORE the threat catalogue.
The evidence chain in this repository starts at a class of published exploit. That is a
LAGGING denominator: it can only contain what has already happened to somebody. It cannot
answer 'what if we failed to write a property before anyone thought of the threat'.
This is the leading one. Enumerate what the system holds or decides that anyone could lose,
cross it with the ways a thing can be lost, and every cell must resolve to a threat class
already in threats.json, or to an explicit out-of-scope with a reason, or be OPEN.
It is enumerable from the DESIGN rather than from the historical record, so it can name a
cell nobody has ever exploited. That is the whole point of having it.
Checked by .github/scripts/assurance/asset_closure.py: every threat id named here must
exist in threats.json, and every cell must carry a status.

loss_modes.theft: value leaves the owner and reaches someone else
loss_modes.freeze: value stays where it is and nobody can move it
loss_modes.dilution: value stays nominally intact and is worth less
loss_modes.misdirection: value moves where it was not meant to, without an attacker profiting
loss_modes.griefing: no value moves and the owner pays anyway, in gas or in a denied service

assets.what: the input a caller has handed over and the output not yet delivered, held by the executor for the length of one transaction

freeze.note: nothing holds value across transactions; a route that cannot complete reverts and returns the input.

dilution.note: the enforced output floor and the caller's own minimum bound how much a route may lose.

assets.what: the standing approval a caller grants the executor or the canonical permit contract, which outlives the swap that motivated it

theft.note: the executor never takes a caller-supplied call target, so an allowance cannot be spent through a route the caller did not sign.

freeze.rationale: an allowance is the caller's to revoke at any time; this system cannot prevent them and does not hold it.

dilution.rationale: an allowance is a permission, not a quantity that can be devalued.

griefing.rationale: a caller who approves and never trades loses nothing but the gas of approving.

assets.what: the share of a swap owed to the treasuries, and the arithmetic that decides it

theft.note: the fee base is re-derived from the on-chain quote of the legs as executed, so a declared figure cannot shrink it.

freeze.rationale: the fee is transferred within the swap; it is never accrued or held pending a later claim.

misdirection.note: the treasury addresses are control-plane state and the control plane can be renounced.

griefing.note: a caller who structures a route so the fee lands in a denomination nobody wants imposes a cost on the recipient rather than on themselves. Bounded and unquantified.

assets.what: which venues discovery serves, which origins are attested, and the fitness ranking that decides what a route may use

freeze.note: after renunciation the registry only grows; what survives that is enumerated and tested.

assets.what: tokens that reach the executor outside a swap - a mis-send, a rebase, a fee-on-transfer residual

theft.note: scaling excludes the pre-swap balance, so a crafted route cannot size itself to funds that were already there.

freeze.note: recovery is a queued, control-plane action and dies with the control plane, which is a deliberate trade and not an oversight.

dilution.rationale: a stranded balance has no share to dilute.

griefing.note: an attacker can strand dust deliberately to make recovery uneconomic. No loss to any user; unquantified.

assets.what: what a caller spends to reach a refusal, including refusals raised by the compiler rather than by a named guard

theft.rationale: gas cannot be transferred to an attacker by this system.

dilution.rationale: gas has no share to dilute.

misdirection.note: three compiler Panic codes are reachable and asserted by no test. A caller meeting one pays for a bare panic instead of a named refusal they could interpret. See panic_inventory.py and panic_sites.py.
